title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Aisha Patel
summary: A single reference for Redwood Inference people managers and people-ops partners describing hiring standards, structured interview process, offer & onboarding checklists, the performance & feedback cycle, and manager responsibilities.
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This guide centralizes Redwood's people operations practices for hiring, employee onboarding (new hire through 90 days), and the performance & feedback cycle. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, and people-ops partners.

Scope:
- Individual contributor and manager hiring across engineering, product, and go-to-market teams
- Standardized interview loops, scorecards, and debriefs
- New hire onboarding checklist and 30/60/90 templates
- Quarterly performance cycles, calibration, and promotion guidance
- Manager responsibilities and escalation paths

Table of contents:
1) Hiring process and standards
2) Interview loop & scorecards
3) Offer process and pre-onboarding
4) New hire onboarding (first 90 days)
5) Performance & feedback cycle
6) Manager playbook & responsibilities
7) People policies highlights and links
8) Templates & appendices

1) Hiring process and standards

Intro:
Redwood uses a structured, evidence-based hiring process to reduce bias, improve time-to-offer predictability, and ensure role fit. The process balances speed with a consistent candidate experience and includes a People Ops partner on all external-facing offers.

Hiring timeline (target):
- Requisition approval: 3 business days
- Sourcing window (active search): 14-30 days depending on seniority
- Interview loop complete: 7-14 days after application screen
- Offer decision: within 48 hours of hiring manager consensus

Key roles & responsibilities:
- Hiring manager: defines role, writes job description, owns interview loop, candidate decision
- Recruiter: sources candidates, coordinates interviews, manages candidate experience
- People Ops partner: compensation & offer approvals, background checks, pre-onboarding logistics
- Panel interviewers: evaluate technical skills, culture add, role-specific skills using scorecards

Requisition checklist (before posting):
- Business case & level justification approved
- Draft job description with core competencies and success criteria
- Interview plan with panel and scorecard assigned
- Compensation band confirmed with People Ops

2) Interview loop & scorecards

Principles:
- Use consistent rubrics and scorecards for each role family and level
- Minimize overloaded interview schedules: max 4 interviews for ICs, max 5 for senior roles
- Separate technical assessment from culture/peer assessment

Standard loop examples:
- IC Engineering (mid-level): Recruiter screen (30m) -> Technical take-home (optional) -> Technical deep-dive (45m) -> System design OR architecture discussion (45m) -> Hiring manager / team fit (30m)
- Manager role: Recruiter screen -> Leadership interview (45m) -> Operational/strategy case (60m) -> Peer interviews (2x30m) -> Hiring manager final

Scorecard fields (one per interview):
- Competency (e.g., coding, system design, product sense) — rating 1-5
- Examples & evidence observed (free text)
- Risks / open questions
- Recommendation: Strong Hire | Hire | Neutral | No Hire

Interview debrief template (use in panel debrief):
1. Candidate name & role:
2. Consensus recommendation:
3. Strengths (3 bullets)
4. Concerns (3 bullets)
5. Calibration notes (differences in ratings and why)
6. Proposed leveling & salary band

Rubric guidance (quick):
- 5: Exceeds expectations with clear, repeatable impact examples
- 4: Meets expectations with strong evidence
- 3: Meets some expectations but gaps remain
- 2: Below expectations; missing key competencies
- 1: Not a fit

3) Offer process and pre-onboarding

Offer approval steps (must complete before verbal offer):
1. Hiring manager submits final debrief and proposed band to People Ops
2. People Ops confirms comp band, equity, and title guidelines
3. Legal / Finance sign-off for any non-standard terms
4. Recruiter extends verbal offer and follows with written offer packet within 24 hours

Offer packet should include:
- Written offer letter (title, base salary, equity, bonus structure if any)
- Summary of benefits and PTO policy link
- Required new hire paperwork and background check instructions
- Target start date and first-week schedule preview

Pre-boarding checklist (before day 1):
- IT: laptop ordered and configured, account provisioning request submitted
- Manager: first-week 1:1s scheduled, onboarding buddy assigned
- People Ops: benefits enrollment window set, payroll forms sent
- Security: access & NDA signed (if required), training scheduled

4) New hire onboarding (first 90 days)

Goals for first 90 days:
- Week 1: orientation, core product context, meet team, technical environment set up
- Month 1 (30 days): contribute to a documented small task, complete learning plan
- Month 2 (60 days): own a feature or operational scope with manager support
- Month 3 (90 days): demonstrate independent delivery and present a 90-day summary

First-week schedule (example):
- Day 0 (pre-start): paperwork complete, laptop shipped
- Day 1: Company orientation (People Ops), team welcome, security & compliance training
- Days 2-3: Deep dives with product and infra owners, environment setup and dev walk-throughs
- Day 4: Buddy pairing and first scoped ticket assigned
- Day 5: 1:1 with manager to set 30/60/90 goals

30/60/90 plan template (manager and new hire fill jointly):
- 30-day objectives (learn): systems, team processes, basic contribution
- 60-day objectives (contribute): execute on a medium-sized task, cross-team syncs
- 90-day objectives (own): deliver end-to-end, identify area for ongoing improvement

Onboarding success criteria (used at 30/60/90 checkpoints):
- Access & tooling: has necessary accounts and dev environment
- Knowledge: understands product architecture and roadmap priorities relevant to role
- Contribution: delivered at least one code/feature/operational change or equivalent
- Cultural integration: regular participation in team rituals and feedback sessions

5) Performance & feedback cycle

Cadence:
- Ongoing feedback: encouraged weekly between managers and direct reports
- Formal check-ins: 30/60/90 for new hires, monthly 1:1s ongoing
- Quarterly performance cycle: goal-setting at start of quarter, mid-quarter check-in, end-of-quarter review
- Annual calibration & calibration cycle for promotions and comp adjustments

Performance ratings & calibration:
- Rating scale: Exceeded Expectations | Met Expectations | Partially Met | Did Not Meet
- Managers submit written calibration notes and evidence for each rating (examples of impact, metrics, peer feedback)
- People Ops coordinates cross-functional calibration calibration meetings to ensure leveling consistency

Feedback best practices for managers:
- Be specific: tie feedback to concrete examples and outcomes
- Balance praise and development: maintain a 3:1 ratio of reinforcement to corrective feedback where possible
- Document feedback: keep short notes in the private manager log for performance history and future calibration

Promotion and leveling guidance (summary):
- Promotion requires evidence of scope increase, repeatable impact, and demonstration of next-level competencies
- Managers should prepare a promotion packet: role expectations, examples of impact, peer endorsements, and proposed new band/title

6) Manager playbook & responsibilities

Hiring & team growth:
- Work with People Ops on headcount planning and job descriptions
- Maintain interview hygiene: use scorecards, avoid overloaded loops

Onboarding & development:
- Ensure first-week schedule, deliverables, and buddy assignment
- Work with direct reports on active development plans and career conversations at least quarterly

Performance management:
- Conduct timely 1:1s and document outcomes
- Run mid-quarter check-ins and create measurable goals with success criteria
- Prepare objective evidence for reviews and promotion packets

People-care responsibilities & escalation:
- Safety & accommodations: escalate to People Ops for medical leave, ADA requests, or harassment complaints
- Performance concerns: for underperformance, follow the informal corrective steps first (coaching plan), then involve People Ops for formal performance improvement plan (PIP) if no improvement after documented coaching

Manager checklist (first 30 days of a new hire):
- Complete role welcome and 30/60/90 plan
- Assign buddy and schedule cross-team intros
- Confirm tooling & access are working
- Schedule recurring weekly 1:1s

7) People policies highlights and links

Key policy reminders (summary lines):
- Time off & PTO: see full policy page for accruals, Unplanned PTO process, and holidays
- Parental & family leave: primary and secondary leave details and benefits
- Compensation & equity: banding, refresh cycles, and promotion-related adjustments
- Code of conduct & anti-harassment: immediate reporting steps and People Ops contact

Appendix: frequently asked questions (short)
Q: Who approves off-cycle offers?
A: People Ops and Hiring Manager (Finance sign-off for anything outside standard bands).
Q: How do I request a remote onboarding buddy?
A: Submit a Buddy Request form to People Ops at least 5 business days prior to start.
Q: Where do I store private manager notes?
A: Use the Teams private manager channel + People Ops documentation repository (restricted access).

Ownership and updates
This page is owned by People Ops. Major updates (policy changes, cadence changes) are published following review by People Ops and two cross-functional reviewers. Minor editorial updates can be made by People Ops without full review.
